docstring:
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?
references: [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ), Erdos50.IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f → ¬∃ x ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, ∃ y > 0, HasDerivWithinAt f y (Set.Icc 0 1) x
